newsitem.title: USA: U.S spot resid prices edge up despite softer crude.
newsitem.headline: U.S spot resid prices edge up despite softer crude.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices mostly edged higher again Friday despite softer crude, boosted by a still-firm gas market and prospects for better utility demand from colder East Coast weather, trade sources said.

"Fuel oil is still zooming. It's still a strong market, and when gas starts getting interrupted, it should even drive resid higher," said one trader, referring to some reductions in gas flows to utilities during peak winter demand.
Strength in bunkers also helped underpin high sulphurs.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent gained a quarter to $21.00-50 a barrel, traders said.
High sulphurs in NYH scored modest gains on still-firm bunkers, with 2.2 percent up slightly at $20.25-50.
NYH 0.3 percent low pour was talked a quarter higher at about $24.00, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent inched modestly higher to $18.50-75, while three percent saw similar gains to $17.50-75.
USG December three percent paper notionally was assessed little changed in the low-$18s despite weaker crude.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.
New York City gate weekend gas tanked 20-30 cents Friday to the $3.40s/mmBtu on prospects for milder weather by Monday. NYH one percent resid was at a $3.37/mmBtu equivalent.
